questions.topic: Link Analysis as a Quality Prior (PageRank)
questions.question: What does PageRank model?
options: Stationary probability flowing along links with teleport restarts
Query-term frequency measured inside a single indexed document
The factual correctness of the claims made on each linked page
The raw count of outgoing links a page places on its own body

questions.topic: Link Analysis as a Quality Prior (PageRank)
questions.question: Why is a source page's PageRank divided by its outgoing-link count?
options: So each target receives the source's complete rank without any splitting
So the source's link-following probability is shared among its targets
So pages carrying several outbound links lose all of their own rank
So the resulting link rank can be read directly as query relevance

questions.topic: Link Analysis as a Quality Prior (PageRank)
questions.question: A links to B and C, B links to C, and C links to A. Starting uniformly, which page receives the most rank after one stated update?
options: A
B
C
All remain exactly equal

questions.topic: Link Analysis as a Quality Prior (PageRank)
questions.question: How are dangling pages with no outgoing links commonly handled?
options: Their accumulated probability is deleted from the system each round
They are excluded from receiving any teleport probability at all
They are given a self-link so their rank stays on the page itself
Their rank is redistributed using the teleport distribution

questions.topic: Link Analysis as a Quality Prior (PageRank)
questions.question: Why should PageRank be a feature rather than a replacement for relevance?
options: It scores query-independent prominence, not topical match to a query
It already accounts for every query term and phrase found in the document
It proves that isolated specialist pages are unreliable as evidence
It cannot be computed at all from a sparse adjacency-list graph

questions.topic: Link Analysis as a Quality Prior (PageRank)
questions.question: Why is observed-graph PageRank not a universal authority score?
options: The damping factor cancels whatever collection bias the crawl may introduce
Crawl scope, missing links, templates, and link farms all shape the graph
Recursive link analysis is provably immune to purchased inbound links
The stationary distribution measures factual correctness of each page

questions.topic: Spam and SEO-Junk Detection
questions.question: Which is a likely content-spam signal?
options: A published corrections policy with named editors and methodology
A concise original methodology section supported by linked data
Extreme keyword repetition beside a thin band of unique content
A stable canonical URL that resolves to the same page over time

questions.topic: Spam and SEO-Junk Detection
questions.question: Why should spam detection combine multiple signals?
options: One repetition threshold separates junk from every legitimate template
Every source type shares one repetition and link-density profile already
Adversaries cannot change their content or their linking behaviour
Any single feature also appears in legitimate pages and can be evaded

questions.topic: Spam and SEO-Junk Detection
questions.question: Thousands of pages share 95% text and differ only by city name. What technique exposes the scaled template?
options: Near-duplicate clustering over normalized text shingles or signatures
Raising the credibility prior on every host that publishes at scale
Scoring each URL independently as its own unit of authoritative evidence
Stripping host and source metadata before the quality features are built

questions.topic: Spam and SEO-Junk Detection
questions.question: Why compare quality features within source type?
options: API references and glossaries never repeat their parameter templates
Legal, reference, and commerce pages are legitimately templated too
Every prose genre shares one link density and vocabulary distribution
Knowing the source type makes adversarial behaviour impossible there

questions.topic: Spam and SEO-Junk Detection
questions.question: How should an LLM quality reviewer be used safely?
options: Let instructions embedded in the page text drive the whole deletion policy
Delete flagged content on one model judgment, keeping no lineage row
Treat page text as data, ask for evidence, and cache versioned verdicts
Execute the scripts a page references so its behaviour can be checked

questions.topic: Spam and SEO-Junk Detection
questions.question: Why is useful SEO not automatically spam?
options: Any publisher who cares about ranking is acting in bad faith already
Structured headings and schema markup prove that a page is factually right
The presence of affiliate links removes all user value from a page
The line is deception versus genuine utility, not interest in ranking

questions.topic: Corpus-Level Dedup Policy: What to Keep and What to Drop
questions.question: What establishes an exact content duplicate?
options: Equal normalized content hashes after boilerplate has been removed
A shared registrable domain between the two candidate documents
Publication dates that fall within one year of one another
Titles that match closely once punctuation has been normalized

questions.topic: Corpus-Level Dedup Policy: What to Keep and What to Drop
questions.question: Which representative is normally preferred in an exact-copy cluster?
options: The scraped copy, since scrapers usually retain the complete text
The authoritative, complete, and access-permitted version
The URL carrying the most parameters, since it is the most specific
The copy whose extraction quality is lowest, to expose the defect

questions.topic: Corpus-Level Dedup Policy: What to Keep and What to Drop
questions.question: A news analysis quotes 60% of a research paper and adds commentary. Why may it remain separate?
options: Similarity rules never apply once two documents sit on different URLs
Any quotation of that length creates an exact-byte duplicate cluster
Its added commentary makes it a distinct information object
The original paper is the one that should be dropped from the corpus

questions.topic: Corpus-Level Dedup Policy: What to Keep and What to Drop
questions.question: Why preserve duplicate-cluster membership and alternate URLs?
options: So every copy in the cluster can occupy its own top-ranked position
So citation-resolution data is cleared once a representative is chosen
So a representative is never replaced when its access permission lapses
So the choice stays reversible and provenance survives the collapse

questions.topic: Corpus-Level Dedup Policy: What to Keep and What to Drop
questions.question: Why can leaving duplicates in RAG be harmful?
options: Copies take several ranks and overweight one evidence lineage
Copies raise the number of genuinely independent corroborations
Repeated chunks lower embedding and prompt-assembly costs
Duplicate sources widen the factual diversity of the context

questions.topic: Corpus-Level Dedup Policy: What to Keep and What to Drop
questions.question: Why must dedup policy be task-dependent?
options: One similarity threshold settles identity for every product and every grain
Legal history, current answers, and propagation need different retention
Every task is best served by keeping only the most recent URL seen
Document revisions never carry distinct effective or valid-from dates

questions.topic: Source Credibility Signals for a Research Corpus
questions.question: Why is credibility claim-relative?
options: One source type is the right evidence for every question that arises
Popularity of a page settles whether its claims can be trusted
A source can be authoritative for one claim and weak for another
Credibility follows from URL structure and domain age alone

questions.topic: Source Credibility Signals for a Research Corpus
questions.question: Which is a useful credibility signal?
options: Anonymous authorship with no stated methodology or data
Affiliate incentives that are not disclosed to the reader
A tracking URL that changes on every visit to the page
Named provenance, cited evidence, and a corrections process

questions.topic: Source Credibility Signals for a Research Corpus
questions.question: For a current Cloud Run limit, which source has the strongest primary-source fit?
options: The current official versioned product documentation page
An undated affiliate post that copies an older forum answer
A two-year-old anonymous comment on a support forum
A vendor comparison page linking unrelated products

questions.topic: Source Credibility Signals for a Research Corpus
questions.question: Why are five sites copying one press release not five independent confirmations?
options: The number of publications has no bearing on corroboration at all
They share a single evidence lineage despite their separate URLs
A press release cannot contain any checkable factual statement
Identical wording shows each publisher verified the claim itself

questions.topic: Source Credibility Signals for a Research Corpus
questions.question: Why store credibility signals separately rather than only one score?
options: Every query intent weights source properties in the same proportion
A single opaque number explains a ranking decision more clearly
Different claims weight primary status, currency, or independence
Separate signals make human review of a source impossible to run

questions.topic: Source Credibility Signals for a Research Corpus
questions.question: How should conflicting credible sources be presented?
options: Show only the most popular source and hide the disagreeing ones
Average the claims into one blended statement without citations
Strip effective dates so the answer reads as a single timeless fact
Preserve the disagreement with sources and their effective dates
